v.why: At alpha near 0.129-1 the network is over-regularized, so reducing the penalty recovers accuracy (runs 14, 20, 18).
Increasing an already large L2 penalty further underfits and lowers accuracy (run 8).
Raising an already large learning rate causes unstable training and big accuracy drops (runs 46, 50).
Lowering a very large learning rate stabilizes training (runs 57, 59, 52).
Very small learning rates undertrain in 243 epochs, so increasing them helps (run 41).
With strong regularization, a smaller learning rate gives a more stable fit (runs 57, 52).
Large learning rates combined with a big penalty collapse training, and a lower penalty helps (runs 20, 14).
Under heavy regularization, larger batches give less noisy updates (runs 27, 23).
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so widening them tends to help (runs 81, 85, 90).
Deeper networks at large learning rates are harder to optimize and often degrade (runs 65, 67, 70).

I based these on patterns in the 100 experiments: high alpha (1, 0.129) is heavily over-regularized, so stepping alpha down there helps a lot (runs 14, 20, 12, 18). High learning rate is unstable, so stepping it up hurts there (runs 44, 46, 50) and stepping it down helps (runs 57, 59, 52). Low learning rate is undertrained, so stepping it up helps (run 41).
